video:video.video:title: How to do 45° Back Extension for Glutes
video:video.video:description: Done the glute way, with a rounded upper back and toes turned out, the 45-degree back extension becomes a hip-extension exercise for your glutes rather than your lower back.

video:video.video:title: How to do Barbell Hip Thrust
video:video.video:description: The hip thrust is the most direct way to load your glutes heavy. Chloe uses it in almost every glute programme because the glutes do most of the work at the top, where squats and deadlifts go easy on them.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Hip Abduction
video:video.video:description: Standing cable abductions train the side glute with constant tension, and the standing position also challenges your balance on the support leg.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Kickbacks
video:video.video:description: Cable kickbacks keep tension on the glute through the whole rep. Chloe also shows the 1 & ¼ version, which adds an extra quarter rep at the top for a stronger squeeze.

video:video.video:title: How to do Gluteator Machine
video:video.video:description: The gluteator is a plate-loaded machine built for hip extension, so the glutes do almost all the work. It's one of the easiest ways to feel your glutes working, especially with the pulse version Chloe shows.

video:video.video:title: How to do Hip Abduction Machine
video:video.video:description: The abduction machine works the side of your glutes, which shape the hips and keep your knees stable when you squat and lunge. Chloe shows both the upright and forward-lean versions.

video:video.video:title: How to do Machine Hip Thrust
video:video.video:description: The machine hip thrust gives you the same glute-building movement as the barbell version without setting up a bar and pad. It's a great choice for beginners and for heavy, controlled sets at the end of a glute day.

video:video.video:title: How to do Machine Kickbacks
video:video.video:description: The kickback machine trains one glute at a time with a smooth, guided path. It's a great finisher after hip thrusts or squats, and an easy way to fix a weaker side.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Leg Hip Abduction Machine
video:video.video:description: Working one side at a time on the abduction machine lets you focus on each glute medius, which is handy if one hip is weaker or your knee caves in on one side.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Leg Hip Thrust
video:video.video:description: Training one leg at a time fixes left-right differences and makes a light load feel heavy. Chloe films it on the machine, but you can also do it with your back on a bench and no weight.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The single-leg RDL builds the glutes and hamstrings one side at a time while training your balance. It's one of Chloe's favourites for shaping the glutes and fixing imbalances.

video:video.video:title: How to do Barbell Squat
video:video.video:description: The barbell back squat is the foundation of lower-body strength. It works your quads, glutes and core together under a heavy load.

video:video.video:title: How to do Belt Squat Romanian Deadlift
video:video.video:description: Doing RDLs on the belt squat machine loads your hips through the belt, so your back and grip get a rest while your hamstrings and glutes still work hard.

video:video.video:title: How to do Belt Sumo Squat
video:video.video:description: The belt squat hangs the weight from your hips, so your legs and glutes get a heavy workout with no load on your spine. A wide sumo stance brings in the glutes and inner thighs.

video:video.video:title: How to do Bodyweight Lunges
video:video.video:description: The forward lunge is a simple, equipment-free way to build leg strength and balance. Tarek shows the alternating bodyweight version, stepping forward with one leg and then the other.

video:video.video:title: How to do Bodyweight Squat
video:video.video:description: The bodyweight squat is where every strong pair of legs starts. Tarek uses it to teach squat form and as a quick conditioning exercise you can do anywhere.

video:video.video:title: How to do Bulgarian Split Squat
video:video.video:description: The Bulgarian split squat is one of the hardest and most effective leg exercises you can do with dumbbells. Your back foot rests on a bench, so the front leg does almost all the work.

video:video.video:title: How to do Deficit Romanian Deadlift
video:video.video:description: Standing on a small platform lets you lower further in a Romanian deadlift, giving the hamstrings and glutes a bigger stretch. It's an advanced variation for people who already hinge well.

video:video.video:title: How to do Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The dumbbell RDL teaches the hip hinge with a lighter, more forgiving setup than the barbell. Chloe shows a normal and a wide-stance version, which brings in more inner thigh and glute.

video:video.video:title: How to do Dumbbell Split Squat
video:video.video:description: The split squat is a stationary lunge: your feet stay in place while you lower and rise. It builds the legs one at a time and is easier to balance than a walking lunge.

video:video.video:title: How to do Hack Squat
video:video.video:description: The hack squat machine guides your body along a fixed track, so you can push your quads hard without balancing a bar. It's a staple quad builder for both Tarek's and Chloe's clients.

video:video.video:title: How to do Heel-Elevated Barbell Squat
video:video.video:description: Raising your heels on a wedge or small plates lets your knees travel further forward, so you can squat deeper with a more upright chest. The result is more quad work.

video:video.video:title: How to do Heel-Elevated Dumbbell Squat
video:video.video:description: With a dumbbell in each hand at your sides (a suitcase hold), you can load heavier than a goblet squat while the raised heels keep the focus on your quads.

video:video.video:title: How to do Heel-Elevated Goblet Squat
video:video.video:description: Holding one dumbbell at your chest with your heels raised is the easiest way to learn a deep, upright squat, and it makes your quads work hard with a light weight.

video:video.video:title: How to do Leg Extension
video:video.video:description: The leg extension isolates the quads like nothing else. It's ideal for finishing a leg day, warming up the knees, or building the front of the thighs.

video:video.video:title: How to do Leg Press
video:video.video:description: The leg press lets you load your legs heavily with your back supported. Chloe shows three foot positions, each one shifting the work to a different part of the legs.

video:video.video:title: How to do Lying Leg Curl
video:video.video:description: The lying leg curl isolates the hamstrings by bending the knee against resistance. It pairs well with Romanian deadlifts, which work the hamstrings at the hip.

video:video.video:title: How to do Pendulum Squat
video:video.video:description: The pendulum squat swings in an arc, keeping tension on your quads even at the bottom. It lets you squat very deep with your back fully supported.

video:video.video:title: How to do Romanian Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The Romanian deadlift (RDL) is the classic hamstring and glute builder. You hinge at the hips with almost straight legs, so the back of your legs gets a deep, heavy stretch.

video:video.video:title: How to do Seated Calf Raise
video:video.video:description: With your knees bent, the seated calf raise targets the soleus, the deeper calf muscle that adds width to your lower leg.

video:video.video:title: How to do Seated Leg Curl
video:video.video:description: The seated leg curl works the hamstrings in a stretched position because your hips are bent. It's one of the best machines for building the back of the thighs.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Leg Leg Curl
video:video.video:description: Curling one leg at a time makes each hamstring work on its own, which helps if one side is weaker or tighter. Chloe shows it on the seated machine.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Leg Leg Extension
video:video.video:description: Doing leg extensions one leg at a time lets you fix strength differences between your legs and focus on each quad.

video:video.video:title: How to do Standing Calf Raise
video:video.video:description: Standing calf raises build the big calf muscle you see from behind. Tarek shows them on the machine, but a step and a dumbbell work too.

video:video.video:title: How to do Stiff-Leg Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The stiff-leg deadlift keeps your legs straighter than an RDL, putting even more stretch on the hamstrings. Chloe demonstrates it with dumbbells.

video:video.video:title: How to do Walking Lunges
video:video.video:description: Walking lunges build the legs and glutes while you travel forward, adding balance and conditioning. Chloe demonstrates them holding dumbbells.

video:video.video:title: How to do Barbell Row
video:video.video:description: The barbell row builds a thick, strong back and teaches you to hold a hip hinge under load.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Rope Standing Row
video:video.video:description: Standing and pulling a rope at chest height works the upper back and rear shoulders, which improves posture and balances out all the pushing we do.

video:video.video:title: How to do Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
video:video.video:description: Lying chest-down on an incline bench takes your lower back out of the row, so you can focus purely on squeezing your upper back.

video:video.video:title: How to do Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The deadlift is the king of full-body strength. You lift a loaded bar from the floor using your legs, hips and back together, which builds strength you'll feel in every other lift.

video:video.video:title: How to do Deficit Deadlift
video:video.video:description: Standing on a platform makes the bar start lower, so you have to pull through a longer range. It's an advanced way to build strength off the floor.

video:video.video:title: How to do Lat Pulldown
video:video.video:description: The lat pulldown builds the wide back muscles that give you a V-shape. It's also the best way to build towards your first pull-up.

video:video.video:title: How to do Pull-Up
video:video.video:description: The pull-up is the ultimate upper-body bodyweight test. Tarek uses it with clients as both a strength goal and a back builder.

video:video.video:title: How to do Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
video:video.video:description: Turning your palms to face you on the pulldown brings your biceps in and lets the lats work through a long range, especially the lower lats.

video:video.video:title: How to do Seated Cable Row
video:video.video:description: The seated cable row builds the middle of your back with smooth, constant tension, and it's easy to learn.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
video:video.video:description: The single-arm dumbbell row lets each side of your back work on its own through a long range. It's simple, safe and one of the best back builders there is.

video:video.video:title: How to do Straight-Arm Pulldown
video:video.video:description: The straight-arm pulldown works the lats without the biceps helping, so it's perfect for learning to feel your back working. Chloe shows it on the cable.

video:video.video:title: How to do Sumo Deadlift
video:video.video:description: The sumo deadlift uses a wide stance with your hands inside your knees. It keeps your torso more upright than a conventional deadlift and works the glutes and inner thighs more.

video:video.video:title: How to do Underhand Barbell Row
video:video.video:description: Flipping your grip so your palms face up lets you pull with your elbows closer to your body, which brings in more of the lats and biceps.

video:video.video:title: How to do Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
video:video.video:description: A wider grip on the pulldown bar puts more focus on the upper and outer lats, the muscles that make your back look wide.

video:video.video:title: How to do Chest Dip
video:video.video:description: Leaning forward on dips shifts the work to your lower chest. Tarek uses them with clients at every level, using the assisted machine for beginners.

video:video.video:title: How to do High-to-Low Cable Fly
video:video.video:description: The high-to-low cable fly sweeps your arms down and together, targeting the lower chest with constant tension. Tarek shows it on a dual-cable machine.

video:video.video:title: How to do Push-Up
video:video.video:description: The push-up builds your chest, shoulders and triceps and trains your core at the same time. Tarek uses it as a strength test and a quick finisher.

video:video.video:title: How to do Smith Machine Bench Press
video:video.video:description: The Smith machine bench press guides the bar on a fixed track, so you can train your chest heavy and safely without a spotter.

video:video.video:title: How to do Smith Machine Incline Press
video:video.video:description: Pressing on an incline targets the upper chest, which fills out the top of your chest near the collarbones.

video:video.video:title: How to do Arnold Press
video:video.video:description: Named after Arnold Schwarzenegger, this press adds a twist: you start with palms facing you and rotate them forward as you press, working the front and side of the shoulders through a long range.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Rear Delt Fly
video:video.video:description: The cable rear delt fly targets the back of the shoulders, which round out your shoulder shape from the side and help posture.

video:video.video:title: How to do Dumbbell Lateral Raise
video:video.video:description: The lateral raise is the best exercise for wider, rounder shoulders. It works the side delts, which no pressing movement fully covers.

video:video.video:title: How to do Front Raise
video:video.video:description: The front raise isolates the front of the shoulders. Tarek shows the alternating dumbbell version and Chloe the EZ-bar version.

video:video.video:title: How to do Machine Shoulder Press
video:video.video:description: The shoulder press machine lets you press heavy with your back supported and no balancing. Chloe shows both the weight-stack and plate-loaded versions.

video:video.video:title: How to do Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
video:video.video:description: The seated dumbbell shoulder press builds strong, rounded shoulders. The back support keeps your body still so your shoulders do the work.

video:video.video:title: How to do Alternating Dumbbell Curl
video:video.video:description: Curling one arm at a time lets you focus on each biceps while the other arm rests briefly.

video:video.video:title: How to do Barbell Curl
video:video.video:description: The barbell curl is the classic biceps builder. Both arms work together, so you can lift heavier than with dumbbells.

video:video.video:title: How to do Bayesian Cable Curl
video:video.video:description: The Bayesian curl faces away from the cable so your arm starts behind your body, stretching the biceps fully. It's one of the best biceps builders around.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Curl
video:video.video:description: Cable curls keep constant tension on the biceps from top to bottom. Tarek shows the single-arm version.

video:video.video:title: How to do Cable Rope Hammer Curl
video:video.video:description: The rope hammer curl on a cable keeps tension on your arms through the whole rep, building the biceps, brachialis and forearms.

video:video.video:title: How to do Dumbbell Bicep Curl
video:video.video:description: The dumbbell curl lets each arm work on its own and rotate naturally, which gives a strong biceps squeeze. Chloe and Tarek both demonstrate it.

video:video.video:title: How to do Hammer Curl
video:video.video:description: Holding the dumbbells like hammers (palms facing in) builds the muscles that make your arms look thicker from the front and side.

video:video.video:title: How to do Incline Dumbbell Curl
video:video.video:description: Sitting back on an incline bench lets your arms hang behind you, stretching the long head of the biceps for a big squeeze.

video:video.video:title: How to do Machine Preacher Curl
video:video.video:description: The preacher curl machine locks your upper arms against a pad so your biceps can't cheat.

video:video.video:title: How to do Reverse Curl
video:video.video:description: Curling with your palms facing down builds your forearms and the muscles beside your biceps, which improves grip and arm thickness.

video:video.video:title: How to do Spider Curl
video:video.video:description: Lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight makes the biceps work hardest at the top. Tarek shows a hammer-grip version.

video:video.video:title: How to do Wide Dumbbell Curl
video:video.video:description: Curling the dumbbells out wide, away from your body, puts more emphasis on the inner (short) head of the biceps.

video:video.video:title: How to do Wide-Grip Bicep Curl
video:video.video:description: Taking a wider grip on the bar shifts more of the work to the short (inner) head of the biceps.

video:video.video:title: How to do Bench Dip
video:video.video:description: Bench dips are a simple way to work your triceps with just a bench. Tarek shows them as a finisher.

video:video.video:title: How to do Diamond Push-Up
video:video.video:description: Bringing your hands together in a diamond shape turns the push-up into a triceps builder.

video:video.video:title: How to do Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
video:video.video:description: Taking your arms overhead stretches the long head of the triceps, the biggest part of the muscle. It's one of the best exercises for bigger arms.

video:video.video:title: How to do Reverse-Grip Tricep Pushdown
video:video.video:description: Turning your palms up on the pushdown shifts more work to the medial head of the triceps and gives your elbows a different angle.

video:video.video:title: How to do Rope Tricep Pushdown
video:video.video:description: Using a rope for pushdowns lets you spread your hands apart at the bottom, giving the triceps an extra-strong squeeze.

video:video.video:title: How to do Single-Arm Tricep Pushdown
video:video.video:description: Single-arm pushdowns let each triceps work on its own and let you find the angle that feels best. Tarek shows a side view, a close-up and the handle version.

video:video.video:title: How to do Tricep Pushdown
video:video.video:description: The tricep pushdown is the go-to cable exercise for the back of the arms. Chloe shows it with a straight bar and a variation.

video:video.video:title: How to do Crunch
video:video.video:description: The crunch is a short, focused abs exercise. Tarek shows it on a decline bench, which makes the same movement harder.

video:video.video:title: How to do Decline Sit-Up
video:video.video:description: The decline bench makes sit-ups harder because you lift your body against gravity through a longer range. Tarek shows bodyweight and medicine ball versions.

video:video.video:title: How to do Hanging Knee Raise
video:video.video:description: Hanging knee raises are the stepping stone to leg raises. Bending your knees makes the lift easier while still working the lower abs hard.

video:video.video:title: How to do Hanging Leg Raise
video:video.video:description: Hanging leg raises are one of the hardest abs exercises. You lift straight legs while hanging, which takes strong abs and grip.

video:video.video:title: How to do Lying Leg Raise
video:video.video:description: Lying leg raises work the lower abs without needing to hang. Tarek shows them on a bench, holding behind his head for support.

video:video.video:title: How to do Sit-Up
video:video.video:description: The sit-up trains your abs through a full range. Tarek shows the bodyweight version and a harder one holding a medicine ball.

video:video.video:title: How to do Superman
video:video.video:description: The Superman strengthens the muscles along your spine and your glutes with no equipment. It's a simple way to balance out all the abs work.
